notes: Read the entire unit, full Iraq-war and counterterrorism context, all three candidates and the review. Preserved the platform's evaluative description of Bush-era global-war rhetoric, and replaced both vague shift references with President Obama's stated move from that rhetoric to a focused effort against al-Qaeda and affiliates. Named the Bush administration and anchored Republican deployment preferences to the 2012 platform.

claims.claim_text: President Obama moved from Bush-administration rhetoric about a global war on terrorism, characterized as sweeping and internationally divisive, to a focused effort against al-Qaeda and affiliates.
That move to focus on al-Qaeda and affiliates is credited with enabling more precise force against people seeking to harm Americans or attack the United States.
It is also credited with enabling movement away from large deployments characteristic of the Bush administration and favored by many Republicans in 2012.
